clue.text: Nothing's missed by card sharp

indicators.note: the card goes without its nothing, so that letter is dropped from it

parts.note: a tarot is a fortune-telling card
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A card cheat who never misses a trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Card sharp' reads as one phrase, a cheat at cards, but 'sharp' is the definition on its own. Like the other down answers, this is also a dish you might see on a menu.
explanation.definitionFit: A tart flavour is acidic and biting, the same taste a sharp one has.

clue.text: Stout men put up walls of lovely old college

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up means reading it from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: OR (other ranks) is the military abbreviation for ordinary soldiers, so men

indicators.note: the walls of a word are its outside letters, first and last

parts.note: a poly was a British polytechnic, a type of college that no longer exists under that name

explanation.surface: Portly men erect the walls of a lovely old college building.
explanation.walkthrough: A roly-poly is also a British jam pudding, fitting the menu theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Roly-poly describes someone plump and round, which is what stout means of a person.

clue.text: Second track Queen's put out — it's like the Beatles

indicators.note: the queen is ejected from the track, so her letter goes

parts.note: a course is a track, as in a racecourse
R stands for Regina, the queen

explanation.surface: The Queen song is dropped from a second track — that's so Beatles.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beatles came from Liverpool; Scouse is the Liverpool accent and people, and also a Liverpool stew.
explanation.definitionFit: Scouse means Liverpudlian, and the Beatles are the most famous Liverpudlians, so anything like them is Scouse.

clue.text: What convicts do half-heartedly, wanting cash by bank

indicators.note: the heart of the word is its double O; doing it by halves keeps only one of them

parts.note: someone wanting cash is poor
a ridge is a raised bank of earth

explanation.surface: Prisoners lazily go short of money near a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang, doing porridge means serving a prison sentence; porridge is also a breakfast oat dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Porridge is British slang for time in prison, so it is what convicts serve.

clue.text: Right back providing extremely loose play

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: providing means if, on condition that

indicators.note: the extremes of the word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A right-back offering very loose play on the football pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right back' looks like a football position, but it splits: Right reversed, then 'providing'.
explanation.definitionFit: To trifle with something is to toy with it, which is to play with it.

clue.text: Charlie following ladies around

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the whole combination round

parts.note: the ladies is the women's toilet, and loo is British for toilet
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A man named Charlie trailing after some women.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie is British slang for a fool, as in 'a right charlie'. A fool is also a fruit-and-cream pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a charlie is a silly person, an idiot.

clue.text: Predicament about marine predator in holiday resort

indicators.note: about here means turned round

parts.note: a jam is a tight spot, a predicament
the orca, or killer whale, hunts at sea

explanation.surface: A tricky situation involving a killer whale at a seaside resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Majorca is a Spanish Mediterranean island, a hugely popular holiday destination.

clue.text: Backing rich man with problem round old French house

indicators.note: backing means everything built is read backwards

parts.note: a nob is a wealthy or upper-class person

indicators.note: the problem goes round the old, enclosing it

parts.note: rub means a difficulty, as in 'there's the rub'

explanation.surface: A wealthy man with a problem supporting an old French house.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bourbons were the royal dynasty that ruled France; house here means a royal family line.

clue.text: What remainers do, eg accepting Brexit ultimately

indicators.note: the example takes in a letter, holding it inside

parts.note: say is used like eg, for example

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Remain voters, for instance, coming round to Brexit in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Brexit referendum, remainers wanted Britain to stay in the European Union.
explanation.definitionFit: Remainers stay where they are; to remain is to stay, so staying is what they do.

clue.text: Cavalier and knight stopping a flu cure working

indicators.note: the knight plugs a gap inside the rearranged letters
a cure working is being put into action, so its letters, with a flu, are reworked

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A careless knight interrupts a working cure for flu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cavalier' looks like a Royalist knight, partnering 'knight', but it is the definition: offhand.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalier attitude is casual and offhand, showing a lack of care.

clue.text: Welsh Church's plan to secure good deal on energy

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed after
the plan wraps round and secures the good deal

parts.note: a chart is a plan or map
a lot means a good deal, a large amount
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A Welsh church plans to land a good energy deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Church is the surname: Charlotte Church is a Welsh singer. A charlotte is also a fruit pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte Church is a famous Welsh singer, so her first name stands for her here.

clue.text: Dolly, perhaps, was 151?

parts.note: Dolly the sheep was a genetic copy, and 151 in Roman numerals reads as CL followed by one

explanation.surface: Was Dolly the sheep number 151 in some series?
explanation.walkthrough: Dolly the sheep, born in Scotland in 1996, was the first mammal cloned from an adult cell; the number splits as Roman 150 plus the word for 1.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolly the sheep was a genetic copy of another animal, the first such mammal; 'perhaps' marks her as an example.

clue.text: British racer keeping ahead in this kind of car

indicators.note: the runner keeps hold of the other letters inside him

parts.note: Seb Coe is a British former Olympic middle-distance runner
up means ahead, as in being up in a match

explanation.surface: A British racing driver staying in front in this sort of car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racer' suggests a motor racing driver, but it is the runner Coe. A coupe is also a dessert of ice cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupe is a two-door car with a fixed roof, a type of vehicle.

clue.text: One concealing fancy undies, mostly, in public

indicators.note: the one wraps round and hides the rest

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate, so these letters are rearranged
mostly means all but the last letter is used

explanation.surface: Someone hiding their fancy underwear while out in public.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the last letter of 'undies' leaves UNDIE, which 'fancy' rearranges into UDIEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The public, as a noun, can mean the people watching or listening: an audience.

clue.text: Cloth seller plugging jacket of cashmere

indicators.note: the seller fills a hole between the other letters
the jacket of a word is its outside, the first and last letters

parts.note: a rep, a sales representative, sells goods

explanation.surface: A cloth salesman promoting a cashmere jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plugging' suggests a salesman advertising, but it means filling a hole. A crepe is also a thin pancake.
explanation.definitionFit: Crepe is a light fabric with a crinkled surface, a kind of cloth.

clue.text: Boxer, you heard, punching cook

indicators.note: the sound punches its way into the middle of the cooking word

parts.note: to fry is to cook

indicators.note: heard tells us to take the word by its sound

parts.note: the word you, said aloud, sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: A boxer, you hear, has thumped a cook.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyson Fury is a British heavyweight boxing champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyson Fury is a world heavyweight champion boxer, so Boxer defines his surname.

clue.text: Salient, good point following a lot of rubbish

indicators.note: the other letters come after the rubbish
a lot of means most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: bull is short for nonsense, rubbish talk
E (east) is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: An important observation, a good point made after a heap of nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salient' looks like an adjective, important, but it is the noun: a military bulge into enemy lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A salient is a part of a battle line that projects into enemy territory, a bulge.

clue.text: Guides have cheese sandwiches with hint of salsa

indicators.note: with here means accompanied by, so the hint of salsa is served alongside, placed at the end
the cheese sandwiches the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: brie is a French cheese
to own is to have

indicators.note: a hint is just the first letter

explanation.surface: Girl Guides eat cheese sandwiches with a touch of salsa.
explanation.walkthrough: Brownies are the junior branch of the Girl Guides; brownies are also chocolate cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Brownies are young members of the Guide movement, so collectively they are junior Guides.

clue.text: What's said to be average appearance

indicators.note: said to be marks a word that sounds like another when spoken

parts.note: the mean is the average of a set of numbers

explanation.surface: What's said to be a person of ordinary looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Mien is a formal word for a person's look or bearing, their outward appearance.

clue.text: Satisfied, engaging a lounge singer

indicators.note: the word engages, holding A within it

parts.note: a demand that is met is satisfied
to loaf is to lounge about idly

explanation.surface: Content, hiring a crooner for the lounge bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lounge singer' reads as one phrase, a bar crooner, but 'lounge' is a verb in the wordplay. Meat Loaf was the American rock singer; meatloaf is also a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat Loaf was an American rock singer famed for 'Bat Out of Hell'.

clue.text: A number on Broadway perform in new titles

indicators.note: in places the performing word inside the other letters
new means the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: to do is to perform

explanation.surface: A Broadway song performed with new titles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let's Do It' is a Cole Porter song first heard in a Broadway musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Let's Do It is a Cole Porter song from the 1928 Broadway show Paris, so a stage number.

clue.text: Model Jean, losing weight, is a diminutive sort

indicators.note: losing means the weight is removed

parts.note: Jean Shrimpton was a famous English fashion model of the 1960s
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Model Jean, after a diet, is now a tiny person.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean Shrimpton was a top 1960s English model. A shrimp is also seafood on the menu.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrimp is an informal word for a small, slight person, the way a tiddler is.

clue.text: Pair maybe 200 metres beyond Belgium's capital

indicators.note: beyond means coming after
the capital of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the 200 metres is an example of a race in athletics

explanation.surface: A couple perhaps travel 200 metres further than Brussels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belgium's capital' wants to be Brussels; it is the first letter of Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace is a set of two, used especially of game birds, so it means a pair.

clue.text: Family member knocked over that Parisian porcelain

indicators.note: in a down clue, knocked over means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: a sib, or sibling, is a brother or sister
que is French for that, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: A relative knocked over that French porcelain ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: Bisque is also a rich seafood soup, fitting the menu theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Bisque is unglazed porcelain fired once, used for figurines and doll heads.

clue.text: Newcomers in clothing of Stockport FC

indicators.note: the clothing of a word is what covers it, its first and last letters

parts.note: Rangers is a Glasgow football club, an FC

explanation.surface: New signings in the kit of Stockport's football club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothing' suggests wrapping round the club, but it simply takes the outside of Stockport. Stockport County is an English club; Rangers, a famous Scottish one, stands for 'FC'.
explanation.definitionFit: Strangers are people one has not met, such as those newly arrived in a place.

clue.text: Moderate old Conservatives, after revolution, in nervy state

indicators.note: after a revolution the word has been turned round

parts.note: Wets was the name for moderate Conservatives in Margaret Thatcher's cabinets

explanation.surface: Moderate Tories, after an uprising, are in a nervous condition.
explanation.walkthrough: To be in a stew is to be agitated; stew is also a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A stew is a state of anxious agitation, as in getting into a stew about something.

clue.text: Record-breaking compiler's very relaxed

indicators.note: the compiler breaks into the record, splitting it

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing vinyl record
the compiler is the setter, who refers to themselves as I; compiler's is I am, shortened to I'm

explanation.surface: The setter, having broken a record, is utterly chilled out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record-breaking' looks like one adjective; it splits into the record and the breaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Limp means floppy and lacking firmness, like a body that has gone completely slack.

clue.text: The two of us, informally, showing where all other down answers may be found

definitions.text: The two of us, informally, showing where all other down answers may be found

parts.words: The two of us, informally, showing where all other down answers may be found
parts.note: a casual way of writing 'me and you' doubles as the card listing the dishes, where the other down entries all appear

explanation.surface: We two, casually, point to where every other down answer turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: The two of us is me and you, written informally as ME 'N' U. Every other down answer is a dish: tart, roly-poly, scouse, porridge, trifle, fool and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu lists the dishes, and all the other down answers are dishes.

clue.text: Artist's sudden change of direction, absorbing right tips from Magritte

indicators.note: the change of direction takes the other letters inside

parts.note: to veer is to change direction suddenly

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A painter's abrupt switch of style, borrowing from Magritte.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Vermeer was the Dutch painter of Girl with a Pearl Earring.

clue.text: A pair of names adopted by Zeus? Oddly, this one's for a girl

indicators.note: the letters are taken in by the scrambled god
oddly means the letters are in a strange order

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for name, and a pair gives two of them

explanation.surface: Zeus, strangely, took on two names, one of them for a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like a call for odd letters, but here it means rearranged: ZEUS becomes SUZE.
explanation.definitionFit: Suzanne is a female first name, so it is a name given to a girl.
